blockers.finding: Commercial approval auto-task issuance may reuse a broad operator credential instead of a dedicated least-capability service principal.

frozen_invariants: The internal task issuer is a service principal distinct from the approving human principal.
The AO-ACT task payload issuer continues to preserve the authenticated approving human identity.
The internal service principal uses the existing operator role and the existing action.task.create scope only.
No new role, scope, Recommendation authority, Approval authority, Dispatch authority, Receipt authority, Acceptance authority, or Execution authority is created.
GEOX_INTERNAL_TASK_ISSUER_TOKEN has no operator_token or admin-token fallback in Commercial runtime.
A missing, revoked, unknown, wrong-role, or over-scoped internal issuer principal fails closed before a task subrequest is sent.
The internal issuer credential cannot authorize approval.decide, action.task.dispatch, action.receipt.submit, acceptance.evaluate, telemetry.write, inspection.write, or unrelated mutation scopes.
MCFT implementation, docs, workflows, bootstrap, database roles, and runtime semantics remain untouched.

explicitly_forbidden: MCFT bootstrap or runtime preflight changes

qualification_requirements: bounded inventory and source/config boundary gate
approval business issuer remains the approver while task auth audit uses the dedicated service actor
unrelated mutation scopes denied for the dedicated issuer token
Frozen PR-SEC-1, residual authority, active-runtime regression
